steps.u: Our Discord ticket bot sometimes posts the 'ticket closed' message twice. Can you stop that?

steps.a: on_reaction_add fires for every user who reacts, so two people ticking the box closes it twice. Closing should be idempotent. I'll check the ticket state before closing.

steps.r:
async def close_ticket(channel):
    await db.execute('UPDATE tickets SET status=\'closed\' WHERE channel_id=$1', channel.id)

i.old_string: await db.execute('UPDATE tickets SET status=\'closed\' WHERE channel_id=$1', channel.id)
i.new_string:
res = await db.execute("UPDATE tickets SET status='closed' WHERE channel_id=$1 AND status='open'", channel.id)
    return res.endswith('1')

if await close_ticket(reaction.message.channel):
            await reaction.message.channel.send('Ticket closed')

steps.a: The close now only succeeds for an open ticket, and only the call that actually changed the row posts the message. I did not reproduce the double post against a live Discord server, only in the unit test with two reactions.

reference.summary: Stopped the duplicate 'ticket closed' message: every reacting user triggered the handler. The database update now only matches open tickets and reports whether it changed a row, so only the first reaction posts the message. Verified with a unit test, not against live Discord.
facts: message posted twice when two users react
UPDATE now restricted to open tickets and returns whether a row changed
message sent only when the close succeeded
tests pass; not checked on live Discord

decisions.choice: make the close an atomic conditional update and post only when it changed a row
decisions.reason: that prevents the double post even when two reactions arrive at the same moment, unlike a check in application code
